subject: Looking for statistical consultant for winter quarter

messages.author: 7e208d26917e9ea2
messages.subject: Looking for statistical consultant for winter quarter
parts:
Dear stats-savvy students,

Are you a senior graduate student who is interested in an opportunity to make some extra money this winter quarter while gaining more experience in multivariate data analysis of ecological communities, with the possibility of co-authorship on a paper? If so, read on...

I am looking to hire someone part-time as a statistical consultant/tutor for a project I am working on under a grant from the Solano County Water Agency. The position would be to assist me in analyzing a dataset of aquatic plant species distributions and environmental correlates, with a goal of identifying the most salient drivers of community composition- probably through model selection, but I am open to other methods. I am guessing the workload would be around 10 hrs/week for one quarter. Pay rate would be around $14.75/hr, for up to 270 hrs total. I am looking for someone who has a solid understanding of statistical concepts, is experienced in analyzing multivariate ecological datasets, and is comfortable with R. This person would need to have no more than a 50% appointment already for winter quarter.

If this sounds intriguing to you, please let me know by Monday, Dec.10. I am happy to provide more information.

Thank you,
Emily Peffer

Emily Peffer
PhD candidate
Graduate Group in Ecology
Department of Plant Sciences
University of California, Davis
Office: (530) 752-2667

parts:
I could be interested. I do multi variate statistics for species distributions and community structure and I'm looking for more real-world/management-type experience, but my plate is pretty full next quarter with TAing and analyzing a few other data sets (including one for the CA dept. of water resources).

Would you like to meet and discuss whether I could still be useful to you with a smaller time commitment?

Thanks,

Dave

Population Biology Graduate Group
